title: Session reconstruction heuristics and dashboard lexicon
body:
Purpose:
This note collects heuristics for rebuilding user/session-level context across multi-hop inference requests, aligns a small dashboard lexicon (consistent widget names and quantile choices), and proposes a low-overhead trace sampling strategy tuned for tokenized inference workloads. Target audience: engineers instrumenting runtime, SREs building dashboards, and product analytics owners who need cost-attribution by session.

Summary (one-liner):
We need a reproducible, low-cardinality way to reconstruct a session across asynchronous requests and routing fallbacks that preserves investigatability while keeping tracing telemetry cost within budget. Dashboards should use standardized names and three-tier quantile bands to make runbook playbooks reliable.

Motivation and context:
- Inference requests are often multi-message (chat), batched, or split across routing tiers (hosted -> dedicated fallback -> private). Root cause often requires stitching: which prompt prefix produced a latency spike, and which tenant/route triggered a fallback?
- Current dashboards mix p50/p90/p99 and raw histograms with different labels, making cross-dashboard correlation error-prone.
- Traces are expensive at full sampling rate; naive head-sampling loses context for long-lived multi-message sessions where later messages are the failure symptoms.

Goals:
- Provide a deterministic session reconstruction heuristic that works with existing request ids and minimal extra headers.
- Standardize widget/metric naming and quantiles to reduce cognitive load for oncall and pagers.
- Define a trace sampling policy that maintains causal linkage across hops with bounded cardinality.
- Add lightweight tenant cost attribution signals for dashboarding without full billing joins.

Heuristic: session-id reconstruction (recommended minimal fields)
1) Prefer client-supplied session_id header (x-redwood-session-id) if present.
2) If missing, derive a stable key by hashing: sha1(tenant_id + user_id + conversation_start_ts_rounded_to_minute). This reduces cardinality while still grouping same-conversation traffic.
3) For batched requests that contain multiple conversation ids, emit per-conversation sub-ids in span tags (session.subid) and expose batch_size distribution on dashboards.
4) Propagate session id across internal hops via trace/span tag plus optional sticky-forward header for external clients.
5) When requests are proxied through routing (e.g., fallback model), add a router_hint tag (router.cluster/variant).

Trace anchors and minimal span design (to keep cost low)
- Root span: request.receive (attributes: tenant_id, model_name, session_id, request_id, route_policy).
- Sync span: model.load (GPU allocation + quantization path tag), kv.cache.lookup (kv_hit boolean), batch.window (batch_size, seq_len_avg).
- Async span: downstream.fallback (if a different backend is used), external-call.* (for external tool invocations).
- Add boolean flags rather than high-cardinality strings when possible (e.g., kv_hit: true/false).
- Use a single long-lived session span (session.context) created at first message and referenced by subsequent request spans (references, not parent->child) to keep traces stitchable without exploding sampled-span counts.

Sampling strategy (budget-aware, severity-weighted)
- Always sample 100% of error-level requests (status >= 500 or inference.error=true).
- Head-sample 2% of all requests (deterministic by request_id hash) to collect baseline latency shape.
- Tail-sample an additional 0.5% of long-tail requests where token_count > 1024 OR service_latency_ms > p99_estimated (using a fast estimator). This captures long-running sessions.
- Session-join rule: if any request in a session is sampled, prefer to sample subsequent requests in the same session for up to N minutes (N=10) or M messages (M=6) to keep context. Implement via sampled-session cache with TTL.
- Priority override: if a routing fallback occurs or model-variant fallback triggers, mark session for forced sampling (1-2% enforceable cap across all forced flags).

Dashboard lexicon and widget conventions
- Widget naming conventions (short, consistent):
  * Latency — p50/p90/p99 by model (ms)
  * Token cost — mean token cost by tenant (USD/token est)
  * Batch distribution — count by batch_size (histogram)
  * KV cache — kv_hit_rate by model
  * Session tail latency — sessions with > p99 request
  * Routing fallback — fallback_rate by route_policy and tenant
  * Seq length — seq_len P10/P50/P90 by route/model
- Quantile bands: always show p50, p90, p99; where space permits add p995 for high-stakes models. Use consistent color palette across dashboards.
- Time windows: default 15m with quick toggles for 1h/6h/24h. For cost-facing dashboards default is 24h with 7d compare.
- Correlation anchors: every latency widget must link to a small panel that shows the top 5 tenants by request volume and top 3 models by latency during the same window. This makes drilldowns quick.
- Low-cardinality filters only: prefer tenant_tier, region, model_family rather than tenant_id in high-level dashboards. Tenant_id and request_id available in drilldown views.

Metric definitions (canonical names to instrumenters)
- inference.request.count: counter emitted on request receive (labels: tenant_id, model_name, route_policy)
- inference.request.success.count: counter for successful finishes
- inference.request.error.count: counter for any error states (labels: error_class)
- inference.latency.ms: histogram (buckets tuned for 1ms..60s) with labels tenant_id, model_name, session_id (session_id only low-cardinality/hashed)
- inference.kv_cache.hits: counter
- inference.kv_cache.misses: counter
- inference.batch.size: gauge (aggregate distribution)
- inference.seq_len.tokens: distribution/sample metric (use telemetry summarization to avoid high-cardinality)
- inference.token.cost.estimate: gauge computed in exporter (USD/token estimate per model + tenant multiplier)

Cost attribution shortcuts (dashboard-friendly)
- Compute a rolling approximate cost per session: session_token_count * model_estimated_cost_per_token. Export session_cost_estimate as a sampled gauge for top sessions only (top 1% by token count) to avoid export costs.
- On dashboards show cost heatmap by tenant_tier, not tenant_id. Provide drilldown to tenant_id for billing team only.

Operational runbook hooks (short)
- If p99 latency increases > 2x baseline and fallback_rate > 1% in same window, open incident with tags: obs-latency-fallback. Primary SRE oncall should check KV cache hit rate, batch size anomalies, and recent rollout flags.
- If session reconstruction fails (missing session_id for > 10% of requests), check ingestion proxies for header stripping and update client SDK to set x-redwood-session-id.

Dashboard layout proposal (compact page)
1) Top row: Global traffic (requests/min), p50/p90/p99 latency summary, error rate
2) Second row: Routing/fallback rate, KV hit rate, batch_size histogram
3) Third row: Session tailers (list of sampled sessions with high token counts), cost estimate heatmap by tenant_tier
4) Bottom row: Quick links to traces (sampled) and recent deploy tags.

Implementation notes and instrumentor checklist (for engineers)
- Avoid adding tenant_id as a free-form dimension in high-cardinality metrics; use tenant_tier and hashed_tenant_id only where necessary.
- Ensure all spans include a small set of stable tags: tenant_tier, model_name, session_hash, route_policy, kv_hit.
- Export session-level sampled gauges only for sessions above token threshold or when flagged by forced sampling rules.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- TTL for sampled-session cache: 10 minutes is provisional — does that match typical conversational cadence? Ask product analytics for session length percentile. (Action: @Maya to provide 90th percentile session length by 2025-02-10.)
- How to ensure unique but privacy-preserving session_hash? Suggest using unsigned sha1 truncated to 8 bytes and base64url encode; legal to approve? (Action: Security review.)
- Do we want tenant-tier vs hashed-tenant_id as default drilldown in public dashboards? Early preference is tenant-tier; confirm with GTM.

Appendix: quick queries (PromQL-style pseudo) for dashboard panels
- requests_per_minute: sum(rate(inference_request_count[1m])) by (model_name)
- kv_hit_rate: sum(rate(inference_kv_cache_hits[5m])) / sum(rate(inference_kv_cache_hits[5m]) + rate(inference_kv_cache_misses[5m]))
- batch_size_hist: histogram_quantile(0.90, sum(rate(inference_batch_size_bucket[5m])) by (le, model_name))
- session_tailers: topk(25, sum(rate(inference_latency_ms_bucket{le="60000"}[5m])) by (session_hash)) // pseudo — only works on sampled session gauges

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally pragmatic: aim for immediate deployable defaults rather than perfect signal coverage. We'll iterate after 2-week telemetry run to check sampling ratios and dashboard usefulness.
- Request owners: Ethan (traces & sampling implementation), Maya (dashboards + widget templates), Rafael (cost attribution + billing join).

End of note.
